sources.title: Warren Mastodon
sources.source_type: primary museum specimen account and photograph
sources.locator: Current Warren mount hero photograph; The Annotated Warren Mastodon / Imitation Tusks / Delicate Detective Work
sources.supports: Named Mammut americanum specimen; current skull, paired curved upper tusks and stocky skeleton. Museum reports historical tusk replacements were too long, so historic images are excluded from dimensional guidance.
sources.visual_inspection: Actual current photograph inspected. It is an oblique perspective, not an orthographic measurement.
sources.rights: Museum photograph copyright retained by AMNH; consulted privately only. No photograph or pixels embedded in public asset.

sources.title: Missouri Leviathan: The making of an American mastodon
sources.source_type: primary museum collection account and photographs
sources.locator: Modern specimen lead image; modern Hintze Hall image; What is a mastodon? and Is a mastodon like a mammoth?
sources.supports: Broad feet and mastodon-versus-mammoth distinction in shoulder/back and tusk curvature. Historical assembly/restoration limits are explicit.
sources.visual_inspection: Actual current oblique and low frontal photographs inspected; supports were ignored. No exact measurements inferred.
sources.rights: Museum image copyright retained by NHM; private visual research only. No images embedded in public asset.

sources.title: Mammoth or Mastodon? Our Curator of Paleobiology Answers
sources.organization: Indiana State Museum and Historic Sites
sources.source_type: primary museum curatorial comparison and specimen photograph
sources.locator: Fred skeleton photograph near introduction; comparative paragraphs on tusks, skulls and typical shoulder height
sources.supports: Fred/Buesching skeletal lateral-oblique view; relatively broad flatter mastodon skull, stockier bones and typical 8–10 ft shoulder height.
sources.visual_inspection: Actual Fred mount photograph inspected. A separate photographed life reconstruction was also seen but is not used as fossil, species or coat evidence.
sources.rights: Museum photograph copyright retained by Indiana State Museum; privately consulted, not embedded or copied.

sources.title: Mammut pacificus sp. nov., a newly recognized species of mastodon from the Pleistocene of western North America
sources.authors: Dooley, Scott, Green, Springer, Dooley and Smith
sources.locator: Discussion of mandibular tusks and Conclusions
sources.supports: Mammut americanum has variable lower-tusk occurrence; a generic late-Pleistocene adult without visible lower tusks is not a species-wide absence claim. Prevents confusing the M. pacificus holotype with M. americanum.
sources.visual_inspection: Text consulted only; no paper figure used as a geometry reference.
sources.rights: Article CC BY 4.0 as linked by the publisher. No text excerpt, figure or 3D data embedded in public asset.

use_note: Only facts and qualitative anatomical observations guide original geometry. Public package contains source citations, not the museum photographs, page snapshots, paper figures or downloaded meshes.
